'''Paul Zachary Myers''' (born March 9, 1957) is an American biologist and activist who founded and writes the ''Pharyngula'' science and atheism [[blog]]. He is associate professor of [[biology]] at the [[University of Minnesota Morris]] (UMM) where he works in the field of [[developmental biology]]. He is a critic of [[intelligent design]], the [[creationist]] movement, and [[pseudoscience]].

In 2006 the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' listed Myers's ''Pharyngula'' as the top-ranked blog by a scientist based on popularity. Myers received the [[American Humanist Association]]'s 2009 [[Humanist of the Year]] award and the [[International Humanist Award]] in 2011. The asteroid [[153298 Paulmyers]] is named in his honor.

==Early life and education==
Paul Zachary Myers was born March 9, 1957, in [[Kent, Washington]].<ref name="ContemporaryAuthors">{{cite book |editor-first=Michael J.|editor-last=Tykus|title=[[Contemporary Authors|Contemporary Authors: A Bio-Bibliographical Guide to Current Writers in Fiction, General Nonfiction, Poetry, Journalism, Drama, Motion Pictures, Television, and Other Fields]] |date=2014 |volume=351|publisher=[[Gale Cengage Learning]] |isbn=978-1-4144-9671-9 |pages=312–131 |chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/contemporaryauth0000unse_f6k0/mode/2up |chapter=PZ Myers}}</ref> He said that he has been a "[[science]] [[geek]]" from an early age, gaining an interest in [[zoology]] and [[marine biology]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-01-06 |title=Science Friday: Interview with a Mad Scientist |url=https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2006/1/6/176487/community/Science-Friday-Interview-with-a-Mad-Scientist/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=Daily Kos |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Growing up, Myers attended an [[Evangelical Lutheran Church in America]] (ELCA) church.<ref>Myers, PZ (June 2, 2013). "[http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/2013/06/02/an-atheist-goes-to-church-1stlc/ An atheist goes to church — 1stLC]."</ref> Prior to his [[Confirmation (Lutheran Church)|confirmation]], Myers says, "I started thinking, you know, I don't believe a word of this."<ref name="mad">{{cite journal |last=Mosedale |first=Mike |date=November 23, 2005 |title=The Mad Scientist, interview with PZ Myers |url=http://www.citypages.com/2005-11-23/news/the-mad-scientist/3 |url-status=dead |journal=City Pages |volume=26 |issue=1303 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080802000603/http://citypages.com/2005-11-23/news/the-mad-scientist/3 |archive-date=2008-08-02 |access-date=2007-08-22}}</ref> Now an [[atheist]], Myers comments on his blog about science, education, atheism and religion.<ref name="blight">{{cite web |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2006/03/left_or_right_religion_and_pol.php |title=Left or Right, religion and politics don't mix |access-date=2007-08-22 |date=2006-03-13 |publisher=Pharyngula |first=PZ |last=Myers |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070212034936/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2006/03/left_or_right_religion_and_pol.php |archive-date=2007-02-12 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://thehumanist.org/humanist/09_nov_dec/Myers.html |title=The Humanist - a magazine of critical inquiry and social concern |access-date=2012-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325072458/http://www.thehumanist.org/humanist/09_nov_dec/Myers.html |archive-date=2012-03-25 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Myers graduated from [[Kent-Meridian High School]] in 1975 and subsequently attended [[DePauw University]] in Indiana on a full [[scholarship]].<ref name="mad" /><ref>{{cite web |date=2010-07-25 |title=My week in the Pacific Northwest |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2010/07/my_week_in_the_pacific_northwe.php? |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100727082730/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2010/07/my_week_in_the_pacific_northwe.php |archive-date=2010-07-27 |access-date=2010-07-25 |publisher=[[ScienceBlogs]] |quote=Saturday at 5:00pm on I'll be attending...my 35th high school reunion with a gang of strange people I haven't seen in decades. You aren't invited unless you were also a graduate of Kent-Meridian High School, Class of 1975}}</ref> However, he returned home the next year after his father suffered a [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]].<ref name="mad" /> He then graduated from the [[University of Washington]] in 1979 with [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[zoology]]. Myers drifted away from this field toward [[evolutionary developmental biology]] and obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in biology from the [[University of Oregon]].<ref name="about">"[http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/about/ About PZ Myers]</ref>

==Career==
[[File:PZ Myers at Skepticon 7.jpg|thumb|PZ Myers presents his talk, "You, too, can know more molecular genetics than a creationist!", at [[Skepticon]] in 2014.]]
Myers has taught and researched at the [[University of Oregon]], the [[University of Utah]], and [[Temple University]]. He is currently an associate professor of biology at the [[University of Minnesota]]'s [[Morris, Minnesota|Morris]] campus,<ref name="facultypage">[http://www.morris.umn.edu/academics/biology/faculty/#myersp PZ Myers Biology Faculty] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130330085915/http://www.morris.umn.edu/academics/biology/faculty/#myersp|date=2013-03-30}} from [[University of Minnesota Morris]]</ref> where he teaches [[developmental biology]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 19, 2015 |title=Biology Faculty |url=https://academics.morris.umn.edu/biology/biology-faculty |website=Academics at the University of Minnesota, Morris}}</ref> He is a member of ''Minnesota Citizens for Science Education'',<ref name="mcse">{{cite web |title=MnCSE Scientific Advisory Board |url=http://www.mnscience.org/index.php?id=14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100330074138/http://www.mnscience.org/index.php?id=14 |archive-date=30 March 2010 |work=Minnesota Citizens for Science Education}}</ref> and cultivates an interest in [[cephalopod]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knickelbine |first=Scott |date=1980-03-09 |title=PZ Myers |url=https://ffrf.org/publications/day/pz-myers/ |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=Freedom From Religion Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Berezow |first=Alex B. |date=2013-04-24 |title=The Very Strange World of PZ Myers {{!}} RealClearScience |url=https://www.realclearscience.com/articles/2013/04/24/the_very_strange_world_of_pz_myers_106516.html |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=www.realclearscience.com |language=en}}</ref>

Myers has been active on the internet. He was involved in scientific debates on [[USENET]] surrounding the growing [[creationism|creationist]] movement. He was a founding member of [[The Panda's Thumb (blog)|''The Panda's Thumb'']] blog. In June 2002, he started his website ''Pharyngula.org'', which morphed into a blog now hosted by [[ScienceBlogs]]<ref name="seedmedia">[http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/], ''Pharyngula'', Science Blogs</ref> and Freethought Blogs.<ref name="FTB">[http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/about/], ''About >> Pharyngula'', Freethought Blogs</ref> In 2006 the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' listed Myers's ''Pharyngula'' as the top-ranked blog by a scientist based on popularity.<ref name="Top five science blogs">{{cite journal |year=2006 |title=Top five science blogs |journal=Nature |volume=442 |issue=7098 |pages=9 |bibcode=2006Natur.442....9. |doi=10.1038/442009a |issn=0028-0836 |pmid=16823420 |doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2008, an [[asteroid]] was named after him, [[153298 Paulmyers]], in honor of this work.<ref>{{cite web |last=Medkeff |first=Jeff |author-link=Jeffrey S. Medkeff |date=2008-03-25 |title=PZ Myers and (153298) Paulmyers |url=http://bluecollarscientist.com/2008/03/25/pz-myers-and-153298-paulmyers/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080807174700/http://bluecollarscientist.com/2008/03/25/pz-myers-and-153298-paulmyers/ |archive-date=2008-08-07 |access-date=2008-03-25}}</ref> 

A self-styled "godless [[Modern liberalism in the United States|liberal]]"<ref name="Pzzx">Tagline on [http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula Pharyngula]: "Evolution, development, and random biological ejaculations from a godless liberal."</ref> and outspoken [[atheist]], he is a vocal critic of all forms of religion, superstition, supernaturalism, spirituality and [[pseudoscience]]. He is quoted as having "nothing but contempt" for [[intelligent design]], arguing that it is "fundamentally dishonest".<ref name="mad" /> In 2009 Myers was named the [[American Humanist Association]]'s "Humanist of the Year".<ref name="AHA award">{{cite web |title=American Humanist Association: Humanist of the year |url=http://www.americanhumanist.org/AHA/Humanists_of_the_Year |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717065124/http://www.americanhumanist.org/AHA/Humanists_of_the_Year |archive-date=2012-07-17 |access-date=2013-06-06 |publisher=American Humanist Association}}</ref>

Myers's book, ''The Happy Atheist,'' was published by [[Random House]] in August 2013.<ref name="ha">{{cite web |year=2012 |title=Random House: The Happy Atheist by P.Z. Myers |url=http://www.randomhouse.com/book/203768/the-happy-atheist-by-pz-myers |access-date=2013-07-26}}</ref> It is largely a compilation of previous blog posts.<ref>[[Branch, Glenn]] (August 8, 2013). [http://www.readcube.com/articles/10.1038/500149a "Godless chronicles: Glenn Branch goes for a dip in the antitheologic."]. ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''. Vol 500, p 149.</ref> Voice for its [[audiobook]] version was provided by noted atheist and science communicator [[Aron Ra]].<ref name="aaa2020">{{Cite web |date=17 September 2020 |title=Ask an Atheist Day? Do I want to do this? |url=https://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/2020/09/17/ask-an-atheist-day-do-i-want-to-do-this/}}</ref> Fellow blogger [[Greg Laden]] celebrates "the level of refinement of his writing" and writes that "these essays actually have a different feel to them".<ref>{{cite web |title=PZ Myers is the Happy Atheist – Greg Laden's Blog |url=http://scienceblogs.com/gregladen/2013/06/25/pz-myers-is-the-happy-atheist/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829120323/http://scienceblogs.com/gregladen/2013/06/25/pz-myers-is-the-happy-atheist/ |archive-date=2017-08-29 |access-date=2017-08-29}}</ref>

In April 2015, [[Atheist Ireland]] issued an official announcement, apologizing that they had given Myers public platforms to speak and that now it is "publicly dissociating itself from the hurtful and dehumanising, hateful and violent, unjust and defamatory rhetoric of the atheist blogger PZ Myers... We believe his behaviour is unjust to individuals, increases prejudice against atheists, and is harmful to the promotion of an ethical society based on empathy, fairness, justice and integrity.".<ref>{{cite web |title=Atheist Ireland publicly dissociates itself from the harmful and hateful rhetoric of PZ Myers |date=7 April 2015 |url=http://atheist.ie/2015/04/atheist-ireland-dissociates-from-pz-myers/ |publisher=Atheist Ireland, Executive Committee |access-date=8 April 2015}}</ref>

In 2017, Myers, who formerly considered himself one of the "New Atheists", disassociated himself from the [[New Atheist]] label. Describing the label as being applied "against our protests, because we were all aware that there was nothing new about it. Maybe we were more aggressive, or maybe suddenly people were listening to us, but really, it was the same old atheism with a fancy artisan label". Myers prefers to be simply referred to as an atheist.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/2017/07/31/the-new-atheism-is-dead-long-live-atheism/ |title=The New Atheism is dead. Long live atheism. |date=July 31, 2017 |website=Pharyngula}}</ref>

==''Pharyngula''==
''Pharyngula'' is Myers's personal [[weblog]], promoted as "Evolution, development, and random biological ejaculations from a godless liberal."<ref>[http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula], ''Pharyngula'', Freethought Blogs</ref> The topics Myers covers are eclectic, delving into the non-scientific as well as scientific. While Pharyngula includes many articles discussing breaking science news and research, the blog has become particularly well known for ridicule of [[intelligent design]] and of attempts to insert it into science education. In 2006, the science journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' listed Pharyngula as the top-ranked blog written by a scientist.<ref name="topfiveblogs">{{cite journal |volume=442 |issue=7098 |pages=9 |title=Top five science blogs |date=2006-07-05 |doi=10.1038/442009a |first=Decla |last=Butler |journal=Nature |pmid=16823420 |bibcode=2006Natur.442....9. |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Myers started Pharyngula.org on June 19, 2002<ref name="Alexa">{{cite web |url=http://www.alexa.com/data/details/main?q=Pharyngula.org&url=pharyngula.org |title=Related Info for: pharyngula.org/ |publisher=[[Alexa.com]] |access-date=2006-09-03 |archive-date=2007-03-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312064647/http://www.alexa.com/data/details/main?q=Pharyngula.org&url=pharyngula.org |url-status=dead }}</ref> as an experiment in writing instruction for a class. Students were required to submit mini-essays to be published online. After the project was finished, Myers still had the web-publishing software, and started to use it himself. The blog is named after his favorite stage in [[embryonic development]], the [[pharyngula]] stage. Pharyngula moved to hosting at [[ScienceBlogs]], a project of [[Seed (magazine)|Seed Magazine]], in 2005.

It was hosted on [[ScienceBlogs]] (2005–2011, in full, and 2011–present, in part) and on FreeThoughtBlogs (2011–present). In 2006, the science journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' listed it as the top-ranked blog written by a scientist based on popularity.<ref name="topfiveblogs2">{{cite journal |author=Butler, Declan |date=5 July 2006 |title=Top Five Science Blogs |journal=Nature |volume=442 |issue=9 |pages=9 |bibcode=2006Natur.442....9. |doi=10.1038/442009a |pmid=16823420 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== History ===
According to [[Alexa Internet]], Pharyngula.org was started on June 19, 2002<ref name="Alexa2">Alexa Internet, [http://www.alexa.com/data/details/main?q=Pharyngula.org&url=pharyngula.org Related info for pharyngula.org]; accessed September 3, 2006.</ref> as an experiment in writing instruction for a class. Students were required to submit miniessays to be published online. After the project was finished, Myers still had the webpublishing software, and started to use it personally. The blog is named after his favorite stage in [[embryonic development]], the [[pharyngula]] stage. Pharyngula moved to hosting at ScienceBlogs in 2005.

In 2007, Myers reviewed [[Stuart Pivar]]'s book ''Lifecode'', which argues that self-organization at the [[Embryo|embryonic]] and [[Fetus|fetal]] stages determines the development and final structure of organisms.<ref name="Lifecode at Pharyngula1">{{cite web |last=Myers |first=PZ |date=July 12, 2007 |title=Lifecode |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/07/lifecode.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070907142321/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/07/lifecode.php |archive-date=September 7, 2007 |access-date=2007-08-21 |publisher=Scienceblogs}}</ref><ref name="Lifecode at Phayngula2">{{cite web |last=Myers |first=PZ |date=July 17, 2007 |title=Lifecode: From egg to embryo by self-organization |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/07/lifecode_from_egg_to_embryo_by.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070906043449/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/07/lifecode_from_egg_to_embryo_by.php |archive-date=September 6, 2007 |access-date=2007-08-21 |publisher=Scienceblogs}}</ref><ref name="Scientific American on Pivar">{{cite web |date=20 August 2007 |title=PZ Myers, ScienceBlogs.com's lead blogger, is being sued for libel |url=http://blog.sciam.com/index.php?title=pz_myers_scienceblogs_com_s_lead_blogger&more=1&c=1&tb=1&pb=1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070823162247/http://blog.sciam.com/index.php?title=pz_myers_scienceblogs_com_s_lead_blogger&more=1&c=1&tb=1&pb=1 <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date=2007-08-23 |access-date=2007-08-21 |publisher=Scientific American}}</ref> Myers reviewed the book negatively, stating that the diagrams and ideas in the book arose from Pivar's imagination and had no basis in actual evidence. After some discussion in the comments threads of ''Pharyngula'', Pivar sued Myers for libel.<ref name="Lifecode at Pharyngula1" /><ref name="Scientific American on Pivar" /> Within a week Pivar withdrew the lawsuit, stating that "the real issue got sidelined" and that his problem was more with [[Seed (magazine)|Seed Media Group]].<ref name="City Pages">{{Cite web |title=Monkey's Uncle, City Pages, Sep. 5, 2007 |url=http://citypages.com/databank/28/1396/article15832.asp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930204455/http://citypages.com/databank/28/1396/article15832.asp |archive-date=2007-09-30 |access-date=2007-09-07}}</ref>

In August 2011, Myers and others founded a new blog network, FreethoughtBlogs, to host ''Pharyngula'' and other blogs in the atheist/secular field.<ref>[http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2011/08/freethoughtblogs_the_official.php Freethoughtblogs: The official announcement] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006172714/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2011/08/freethoughtblogs_the_official.php|date=2011-10-06}}</ref> According to Myers, the move was made as an "acceptable compromise" between him and National Geographic, who at that time would be "taking a more active role in hosting the ScienceBlogs stable" and therefore "bringing their standards & practices, which are different from the more freewheeling policies of Seed Media [and would cause] a culture clash". Myers stated that "NatGeo and I have worked out an acceptable compromise. This site on Freethoughtblogs [...is not] in any way associated with National Geographic" and that he would only cross-post to his original site on ScienceBlogs "whatever I write that I feel is compatible with the more conservative ethos of National Geographic."<ref>[http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/2011/07/31/welcome-to-the-new-digs/ Inaugural ''Pharyngula'' post on Freethoughtblogs]</ref> As such, since August 2011, the complete Pharyngula has appeared on FreethoughtBlogs, and a limited selection of those posts – the more science-focused ones – are cross-posted to the ScienceBlogs-hosted version.

In September 2012, Myers announced that blogger and environmentalist Chris Clarke would become ''Pharyngula''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s co-author.<ref>{{cite web |date=September 6, 2012 |title=''Pharyngula'' is about to Add a Co-Blogger |url=http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/2012/09/06/pharyngula-is-about-to-add-a-co-blogger/ |website=Pharyngula}}</ref> Clarke left the blog in August 2013, partly because of the perceived unpleasantness of ''Pharyngula'' commenters <ref>{{cite web |date=September 1, 2013 |title=Farewell, Chris! |url=http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/2013/09/01/farewell-chris/ |website=Pharyngula}}</ref>

=== Content ===
Myers often criticizes intelligent design, creationism and [[pseudoscientific]] movements, and posts on subjects such as science, religion, politics, superstition, and education. His experience in evolutionary developmental biology and as a teacher provides depth to the subjects of science and education.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} One theme that arises regularly is that of [[cephalopods]], creatures that Myers finds quite fascinating.

In particular Myers frequently offers specific criticisms of creationism, including intelligent design as well as the [[Discovery Institute]], [[Answers in Genesis]], and other groups that promote [[Pseudoscience|pseudoscientific]] ideas. For example, in February and March 2007, he focused many of his posts on creationist [[neurosurgeon]] [[Michael Egnor]], who had recently joined the Discovery Institute. In addition to Myers's criticisms of Egnor's arguments on [[evolution]] and Intelligent Design, Myers criticized the Discovery Institute's reliance on someone whose expertise wasn't relevant to evolution.<ref>''[http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/02/dr_michael_egnor_challenges_ev.php Dr Michael Egnor challenges evolution!] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090531055952/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/02/dr_michael_egnor_challenges_ev.php|date=2009-05-31}}'', Pharyngula, 2007-01-18.</ref>

In early April 2007, Myers participated in an [[April Fool's Day]] joke arranged by ''[[The Panda's Thumb (blog)|The Panda's Thumb]]'' which manufactured a website spoofing the Discovery Institute's page on which "Egnor" admitted that his association with the Discovery Institute was itself an April Fool's joke. This elaborate prank succeeded in fooling many of his readers, while others succeeded in spotting jokes in the design of the false Discovery Institute page and concluded that this admission was itself the prank.<ref>[http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/04/01/we-should-have-known-betteregn/ "We should have known better—Egnor fooled us all"], ''Pharyngula'', 2007-04-01.</ref> He made a point the following day that he perceived it as getting exceedingly difficult to believe some creationists were for real (cf. [[Poe's Law]]) and highlighted a quote by [[Stephen C. Meyer|Stephen Meyer]].<ref>[http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/04/02/its-april-2nd/ "It's April 2nd!"], ''Pharyngula'', 2007-04-02.</ref><ref>[http://www.pandasthumb.org/archives/2007/04/the_silliest_th_3.html#comment-167968 "The Silliest Thing Yet, or Sheer Genius?"], ''Panda's Thumb'', 2007-04-02.</ref>

=== Memes ===
Myers has voiced the position that many of the responses to [[Richard Dawkins]]'s ''[[The God Delusion]]'' are what he calls "[[Courtier's reply|Courtier's Replies]]". Replying to critics who felt that Dawkins ignored sophisticated versions of modern theology, Myers compared them to courtiers fawning on the legendary [[The Emperor's New Clothes|emperor who had no clothes]]:

{{quote|I have considered the impudent accusations of Mr Dawkins with exasperation at his lack of serious scholarship. He has apparently not read the detailed discourses of Count Roderigo of Seville on the exquisite and exotic leathers of the Emperor's boots, nor does he give a moment's consideration to Bellini's masterwork, ''On the Luminescence of the Emperor's Feathered Hat.'' We have entire schools dedicated to writing learned treatises on the beauty of the Emperor's raiment, and every major newspaper runs a section dedicated to imperial fashion; Dawkins cavalierly dismisses them all. (...) Dawkins arrogantly ignores all these deep philosophical ponderings to crudely accuse the Emperor of nudity.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2006/12/24/the-courtiers-reply/
| title = The Courtier's Reply
| work= Pharyngula
| author = Myers, PZ
| date = 2006-12-24
| access-date = 2007-07-17}}</ref>}}

In other words, critics complain about Dawkins not studying aspects of theology that are irrelevant to whether or not God exists in the same way as scholarly writings about imperial fashion are irrelevant when the emperor is naked. Dawkins himself quoted the Courtier's Reply in a debate with [[Alister McGrath]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Myers, PZ |date=2007-03-28 |title=The "magnificent P-Zed"? |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/03/the_magnificent_pzed.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070914185839/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/03/the_magnificent_pzed.php |archive-date=2007-09-14 |access-date=2007-07-17 |work=Pharyngula}}</ref> He also referenced the Courtier's Reply in the preface to ''The God Delusion''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s 2007 paperback edition.<ref name="dawkins">{{cite web |date=2007-06-20 |title=Richard Dawkins reads the new preface to ''The God Delusion'' (paperback) |url=http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=-2040224787207865440 |access-date=2007-07-18}} See also {{cite news |author=Dawkins, Richard |author-link=Richard Dawkins |date=2007-05-12 |title=How dare you call me a fundamentalist |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/comment/columnists/guest_contributors/article1779771.ece |access-date=2007-07-18 |newspaper=The Times |location=London}}</ref>

Another recurring [[Trope (literature)|trope]] has been Myers's reaction to the label "fundamentalist atheist", bestowed by some upon him, Dawkins and others who espouse similar views.<ref name="dawkins" /><ref>{{cite web |author=Myers, PZ |date=2007-02-26 |title=The False Equation |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/02/the_false_equation.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070307213536/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/02/the_false_equation.php |archive-date=2007-03-07 |access-date=2007-07-18 |work=Pharyngula}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Myers, PZ |date=2007-04-05 |title=So what should we ornery atheists call ourselves? |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/04/so_what_should_we_ornery_athei.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715220112/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/04/so_what_should_we_ornery_athei.php |archive-date=2007-07-15 |access-date=2007-07-18 |work=Pharyngula}}</ref> Myers summarizes his stance by invoking "Blake's Law", named for ''Pharyngula'' commentator Blake Stacey.<ref name="molly">{{cite web |author=Myers, PZ |year=2007 |title=Commenter Awards |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/molly.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070708060233/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/molly.php |archive-date=2007-07-08 |access-date=2007-07-17 |work=Pharyngula}}</ref> As formulated by Stacey in 2007, based in concept on [[Godwin's Law]]: "In any discussion of atheism (skepticism, etc.), the probability that someone will compare a vocal atheist to religious fundamentalists increases to one."<ref name="Science after Sunclipse">{{cite web |author=Stacey, Blake |date=2007-04-05 |title=Recycled Blake Stacey: Following Godwin's Example |url=http://www.sunclipse.org/?p=18 |access-date=2007-07-17}}</ref> He writes,<blockquote>The "[[new atheism]]" (I don't like that phrase, either) is about taking a core set of principles that have proven themselves powerful and useful in the scientific world — you've probably noticed that many of these uppity atheists are coming out of a scientific background — and insisting that they also apply to everything else people do. These principles are a reliance on natural causes and demanding explanations in terms of the real world, with a documentary chain of evidence, that anyone can examine. The virtues are critical thinking, flexibility, openness, verification, and evidence. The sins are dogma, faith, tradition, revelation, superstition, and the supernatural. There is no holy writ, and a central idea is that everything must be open to rational, evidence-based criticism — it's the opposite of fundamentalism.<ref>{{cite web |author=Myers, PZ |date=2007-06-14 |title=High Priest Epstein in ''Newsweek'' |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/06/high_priest_epstein_in_newswee.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070617004155/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/06/high_priest_epstein_in_newswee.php |archive-date=2007-06-17 |access-date=2007-07-18 |work=Pharyngula}}</ref></blockquote>Myers has made frequent use of the phrase "deep rifts" to satirize perceptions that atheism could experience a [[Schism (religion)|religious schism]] over disagreements on marketing atheism or the role of science and religion. Myers does not deny there are some differences of opinion between prominent atheists, but contends this is a good thing and is attributed to the [[Freethought|freethinking]] nature of atheism.<ref name="pharyngula">{{cite web |author=Myers, PZ |author-link=PZ Myers |date=2009-11-09 |title=The Deep Rifts simply call us unto the breach once more |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2009/11/09/the-deep-rifts-simply-call-us/ |access-date=2013-11-09 |work=Pharyngula}}</ref>

===Eucharist incident===
{{see also|Host desecration#2008 controversy in the US|Catholic League (U.S.)#Eucharist incident}}

{{wikinews|Woman fired over husband's email threat to Minnesota professor|date=July 16, 2008}}A controversy arose in July 2008 over a Pharyngula blog entry written by Myers expressing amazement at news reports of [[death threat]]s issued to [[University of Central Florida]] Student Senator Webster Cook.<ref>{{cite web |date=2008-07-09 |title='Body Of Christ' Snatched From Church, Held Hostage By UCF Student |url=http://www.wftv.com/news/16798008/detail.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080711042722/http://www.wftv.com/news/16798008/detail.html |archive-date=2008-07-11 |access-date=2008-07-11 |publisher=WFTV}}</ref><ref name="Star Tribune">[http://www.startribune.com/lifestyle/faith/24313139.html?location_refer=Entertainment Communion wafer held 'hostage' raises holy heck], ''Star Tribune'', Jul 11, 2008.  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703085006/http://www.startribune.com/lifestyle/faith/24313139.html?location_refer=Entertainment|date=July 3, 2009}}</ref> On June 29, 2008, Cook attended a [[Mass (Catholic Church)|Catholic Mass]] being held in the student union at UCF by a Catholic student group that receives funding from the student government. Cook received the [[Eucharist in the Catholic Church|Catholic Eucharist host]] but did not consume it immediately. He said later that he wanted to take it back to his seat to show a friend, but when stopped he pretended to put it in his mouth until back at his seat, then a church leader made forcible attempts to take the wafer from him.<ref name="FreethoughtRadio">{{cite web |date=2008-07-19 |title=Radio interview with "Webster Cook, student senator and non-eater of communion wafers" |url=http://ffrf.libsyn.com/index.php?post_id=361015 |access-date=2008-07-28 |publisher=Freethought Radio |format=online radio |quote=Tune in to hear the inside story about the young Orlando student whom Catholics have accused of committing a 'hate crime' for not eating a communion wafer!}}</ref><ref name="bodysnatch">{{cite web |date=2008-07-09 |title='Body Of Christ' Snatched From Church, Held Hostage By UCF Student |url=http://www.wftv.com/news/16798008/detail.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080711042722/http://www.wftv.com/news/16798008/detail.html |archive-date=2008-07-11 |access-date=2008-07-11 |publisher=WFTV}}</ref> Cook stored the host at his home, then returned it one week later after receiving e-mail threats and pleas.<ref name="FreethoughtRadio" /><ref name="return">{{cite web |date=2008-07-09 |title='Body Of Christ" Returned To Church After Student Receives Email Threats |url=http://www.wftv.com/news/16806050/detail.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080725000057/http://www.wftv.com/news/16806050/detail.html |archive-date=2008-07-25 |access-date=2008-07-25 |publisher=WFTV}}</ref> [[Bill Donohue]], President of the [[Catholic League (U.S.)|Catholic League]], described the student's actions as "beyond hate speech" and said that "All options should be on the table, including expulsion."<ref name="Don1">{{cite web |date=2008-07-07 |title=Florida Student Abuses Eucharist |url=http://www.catholicleague.org/release.php?id=1458 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110825035803/http://www.catholicleague.org/release.php?id=1458 |archive-date=25 August 2011 |access-date=2008-07-25 |publisher=The Catholic League}}</ref>

In his July 8 blog entry, he asked readers to acquire for him consecrated Eucharistic hosts, which he might "show you sacrilege, gladly, and with much fanfare" and could treat "with profound disrespect and heinous cracker abuse, all photographed and presented here on the web".<ref name="Myers Eucharist">{{cite web |author=PZ Myers |date=2008-07-08 |title=IT'S A FRACKIN' CRACKER! |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/07/its_a_goddamned_cracker.php#more |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080712015833/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/07/its_a_goddamned_cracker.php#more |archive-date=2008-07-12 |access-date=2008-07-11 |work=Pharyngula |publisher=Scienceblogs}}</ref> Bill Donohue's [[Catholic League (U.S.)|Catholic League]] responded with a letter demanding the University of Minnesota and the Minnesota State Legislature take action against Myers. Proponents of this action noted that Myers's blog could be reached from his university web page.<ref name="Star Tribune" /><ref>{{cite web |date=2008-07-10 |title=Minnesota Prof Pledges to Desecrate Eucharist |url=http://www.catholicleague.org/release.php?id=1459 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080713023423/http://www.catholicleague.org/release.php?id=1459 |archive-date=July 13, 2008 |access-date=2008-07-11 |publisher=The Catholic League}}</ref> Myers has received several [[death threats]] and much [[hate mail]] over the [[controversy]].<ref name="Myers death threats">{{cite web |author=PZ Myers |date=2008-07-13 |title=Mail Dump |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/07/mail_dump.php#more |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080714153817/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/07/mail_dump.php#more |archive-date=2008-07-14 |access-date=2008-07-14 |work=Pharyngula |publisher=Scienceblogs}}</ref>

Myers criticized the reaction to Cook's act. Myers described the level of harassment including multiple death threats leveled against the student, and accusations against the student which included [[hate crime]], [[kidnapping]], and intent to [[Host desecration|desecrate the Eucharist]] which Catholics consider a [[mortal sin]].<ref name="bodysnatch" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Getuiza |first=Cheryl |date=2008-07-09 |title=Student Who Took Religious Icon Getting Death Threats |url=http://www.myfoxorlando.com/dpp/news/Student_Who_Took_Religious_Icon_Getting_Death_Threats |access-date=2009-11-18 |publisher=My [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] Orlando}}</ref> Myers expressed outrage that [[Fox News Channel]] appeared to be inciting readers to cause further problems for the student, and ridiculed reports that armed guards would attend the next mass.

Myers was criticized from both religious and non-religious quarters. The Catholic League accused Myers of [[anti-Catholic]] [[bigotry]],<ref name="holyheck">{{cite web |date=July 11, 2008 |title=Communion wafer held 'hostage' raises holy heck |url=http://www.startribune.com/lifestyle/faith/24313139.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204001624/http://www.startribune.com/lifestyle/faith/24313139.html |archive-date=February 4, 2009 |work=Minneapolis Star Tribune}}</ref> described his proposal as a threat to desecrate what [[Transubstantiation|Catholics hold to be the Body of Christ]], and sent a letter asking the University of Minnesota and the Minnesota State Legislature to take action against Myers.<ref name="holyheck" /><ref name="pledge2">{{cite web |date=2008-07-10 |title=Minnesota Prof Pledges to Desecrate Eucharist |url=http://www.catholicleague.org/release.php?id=1459 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080713023423/http://www.catholicleague.org/release.php?id=1459 |archive-date=2008-07-13 |access-date=2008-07-11 |publisher=The Catholic League}}</ref> The Catholic League argued that, as the Pharyngula website was accessible via a link from the University of Minnesota's website, it should be bound by the university's code of conduct, which requires faculty to be "respectful, fair and civil" when dealing with others.<ref name="pledge2" /> Joe Foley, a member of the Board of the [[Secular Student Alliance]], wrote on the organization's website that Myers had "crossed the line" from "playful satire" to "masturbatory condescension".<ref name="SSA">[http://www.secularstudents.org/node/2168 J. Foley, "Wafergate: PZ Myers Crossed the Line"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110406075332/http://www.secularstudents.org/node/2168|date=2011-04-06}}, secularstudents.org, Aug. 3, 2008</ref> Foley concluded, "if open-minded believers are willing to join us in polite dialogue, we need to be ready to welcome them with more than ridicule and pranks".<ref name="SSA" />

Subsequently, Myers explained to the ''[[Star Tribune]]'' that while his post was "satire and protest", he had received death threats regarding the incident but was not taking them too seriously.<ref name="holyheck" /> In a talk show featuring Myers on ''Catholic Radio International'', hosted by Jeff Gardner, Myers confirmed that he had been sent an unspecified number of consecrated hosts and said that he intended to "subject them to heinous cracker abuse". When asked by Gardner to explain why he must do so, Myers said that Donohue of the Catholic League was insisting that he acknowledge the Body of Christ in the Eucharist. Gardner pointed out that Donohue had no authority to insist on such acknowledgment. The show host then asked Myers which individual possessing the [[Magisterium|Magisterial]] authority of the Catholic Church had insisted that he recognize the Body of Christ in the Eucharist. Myers replied that no one from the Catholic Church had contacted him.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Heart Of The Matter On Catholic Radio International{{pipe}}2008-07-10 |url=http://www.catholicradiointernational.com/heartofmatter.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080720221516/http://www.catholicradiointernational.com/heartofmatter.php |archive-date=2008-07-20 |access-date=2008-07-18 |work=We Need To Talk |publisher=Catholic Radio International}}</ref>

On July 24, 2008, Myers, in his post, "The Great Desecration," wrote that he had pierced through the "goddamned cracker" with a rusty nail, which he also used to pierce a few ripped-out pages of the [[Qur'an]] (in English translation, not the original Arabic) and ''[[The God Delusion]]'', and had simply thrown them all in the trash along with old coffee grounds and a banana peel. He provided a photograph of these items in the garbage, and wrote that nothing must be held sacred, encouraging people to question everything. In addition, he described the history of allegations of [[host desecration]], emphasizing the frequent use of such allegations in medieval Europe to justify [[anti-Semitism]].<ref name="TheGreatDesecration">{{cite web |last=Myers |first=PZ |date=2008-07-24 |title=Pharyngula: The Great Desecration |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/07/the_great_desecration.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080725040151/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/07/the_great_desecration.php |archive-date=2008-07-25 |access-date=2008-07-24 |work=Pharyngula |publisher=[[ScienceBlogs]]}}</ref> The following day, University of Minnesota, Morris (UMM) Chancellor stated: "I believe that behaviors that discriminate against or harass individuals or groups on the basis of their religious beliefs are reprehensible" and that the school "affirms the freedom of a faculty member to speak or write as a public citizen without institutional discipline or restraint".<ref>WALSH, PAUL [http://www.startribune.com/local/25896599.html?location_refer=Homepage:latestNews:4 Morris chancellor defends instructor who defiled Eucharist, tore Qur'an] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090827022715/http://www.startribune.com/local/25896599.html?location_refer=Homepage:latestNews:4|date=2009-08-27}} Star Tribune, July 25, 2008</ref>

==Science activism==

===Interview and screening of ''Expelled''===
In April 2007 Myers was interviewed for what he was told would be a documentary titled ''Crossroads'', purportedly about science and religion.<ref name="scienceblogs.com">{{cite news |first=PZ |last=Myers |title=I'm gonna be a MOVIE STAR |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/08/im_gonna_be_a_movie_star.php#more |publisher=[[Pharyngula (blog)]] |date=2007-08-22 |access-date=2008-05-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514090732/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/08/im_gonna_be_a_movie_star.php#more |archive-date=2008-05-14 |url-status=dead}}</ref> However, in September 2007, executive producer Mark Mathis announced that the film was ''[[Expelled: No Intelligence Allowed]]'' about perceived censorship of intelligent design supporters in academia and elsewhere.<ref name=nyt>{{cite news |first=Cornelia |last=Dean |title=Scientists Feel Miscast in Film on Life's Origin |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/09/27/science/27expelled.html?_r=2&oref=slogin&oref=slogin |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=2007-09-27 |access-date=2008-05-28}}</ref> Regarding the discrepancy of focus, Myers wrote: "I mean, seriously, not telling one of the sides in a debate about what the subject might be and then leading him around randomly to various topics, with the intent of later editing it down to the parts that just make the points you want, is the video version of [[quote-mining]] and is fundamentally dishonest."<ref name="scienceblogs.com"/>

On March 20, 2008, Myers was [[Expelled: No Intelligence Allowed#PZ Myers and Richard Dawkins at Minnesota pre-release screening|denied entry into a screening]] of ''Expelled: No Intelligence Allowed'' at the [[Mall of America]] in [[Minneapolis]]. He was waiting with his family and guests to attend a private screening after having reserved seats for himself and guests under his own name using the freely available online procedure set up by the film's promoters. Shortly before the film started, a security guard told him that the producer Mark Mathis had instructed that Myers be removed from the premises. After telling his family of this Myers went to a nearby Apple store and [[blog]]ged about his amusement that they had expelled him, but allowed his guest entry to see the film—British [[evolutionary biologist]] [[Richard Dawkins]], who had also been interviewed for the film under similar circumstances.<ref name=latenightquickone>{{cite web |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/03/expelled.php |title=Pharyngula: EXPELLED! |access-date=2008-03-23 |first=PZ |last=Myers |date=2008-03-20 |quote=There is a rich, deep kind of irony that must be shared. I'm blogging this from the Apple store in the Mall of America, because I'm too amused to want to wait until I get back to my hotel room. I went to attend a screening of the creationist propaganda movie, Expelled, a few minutes ago. Well, I tried... but I was Expelled! |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080322090750/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2008/03/expelled.php |archive-date=2008-03-22 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In a question and answer session at the end of the film Dawkins asked why Myers had been excluded, and later said that "if anyone had a right to see the film, it was [Myers]. The incompetence, on a public relations level, is beyond belief."<ref name=twinc>{{cite web |url=http://www.twincities.com/ci_8653837 |title=Biology prof expelled from screening of 'Expelled' - TwinCities.com |access-date=2008-03-21 |first=Chris |last=Hewitt |date=2008-03-21 |publisher=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press|The Pioneer Press]]}}</ref> The saga has been described by Dawkins as "an incredible piece of inept public relations" on the part of the film's producers.<ref>[http://media.richarddawkins.net/video/2008/RDPZweb.mov Discussion on PZ Myers being expelled from Expelled] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090120212829/http://media.richarddawkins.net/video/2008/RDPZweb.mov |date=2009-01-20 }}. The [[Richard Dawkins Foundation for Reason and Science]]. Retrieved March 22, 2008</ref>

===Creation Museum visit===
[[File:PZ Myers (1).jpg|thumb|Myers at the Creation Museum]]
Myers's engagement as keynote speaker at the 2009 [[Secular Student Alliance]] Conference in [[Columbus, Ohio]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Secular Student Alliance |url=http://www.secularstudents.org/conference |access-date=2009-08-17}}</ref> developed into an August 7, 2009, trip, in which 304 attendees visited the nearby [[Creation Museum]] in [[Petersburg, Boone County, Kentucky|Petersburg, Kentucky]].<ref>{{cite web |title=A firebrand visits Creation Museum |first=Devin |last=Powell |url=http://www.startribune.com/lifestyle/53237252.html |work=StarTribune.com |publisher=Star Tribune |location=Minneapolis |date=2009-08-14 |access-date=2009-08-17 |archive-date=2009-08-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090818143104/http://www.startribune.com/lifestyle/53237252.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Appearances==
Myers has been invited to speak about science, rationalism, or atheism at conferences, symposia, and other events.

* [[Secular Student Alliance]] Conference in [[Columbus, Ohio]], 2009
* [[Glasgow Skeptics]] in the Pub, 2011<ref>{{cite web |title=PZ Myers on the Pharyngula at Glasgow Skeptics | date=10 June 2011 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=115DdMmp2Bw |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/115DdMmp2Bw |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live |publisher=[[Glasgow Skeptics]] |access-date=18 April 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
* [[Global Atheist Convention]] in [[Melbourne, Australia]], 2012
* [[Reason Rally]], 24 March 2012

In July 2013, Freethought Blogs organized an online virtual conference called FtBCon or FtB Conscience. Google+ Hangout software was used to enable real-time discussion around the world. Participants included all the Freethought Blog bloggers as well as Jeremy Beahan, [[Jamila Bey]], Virginia Brown, Ania Bula, [[David Brin]], Eneasz Brodski, Ian Bushfield, environmental blogger and author [[Chris Clarke (blogger)|Chris Clarke]], James Croft, Heina Dadabhoy, [[J. T. Eberhard]], Daniel Fincke, [[Debbie Goddard]], [[Julia Galef]], Nicole Harris, Rebecca Hensler, scientist and blogger [[Greg Laden]], Robin Marty, science artist & blogger Glendon Mellow, Aoife O'Riordan, [[Beth Presswood]] of The Atheist Experience, [[Kim Rippere]], [[Amy Davis Roth|Amy Roth]], [[Jacques Rousseau (secular activist)|Jacques Rousseau]], [[Desiree Schell]] of [[Skeptically Speaking]], [[David Silverman (activist)|David Silverman]], Xavier Trapp, blogger [[Rebecca Watson]], [[Eliezer Yudkowsky]], scientist & blogger [[Bora Zivkovic (science blogger)|Bora Zivkovic]], and others. The conference was free and took place over three days.<ref name=ftbcon2013>{{Cite web |url=http://freethoughtblogs.com/pharyngula/ftbcon/comment-page-1/ |title=FtBCon 2013: Atheism with a conscience |date=2013-06-21 |access-date=2013-07-21 |publisher=Freethought Blogs}}</ref>

==Awards==
Myers has received several awards for his activism and blogging.
* International Humanist Award (2011)<ref name=IHEU>{{cite web |title=IHEU Awards for 2011 |url=http://iheu.org/story/iheu-awards-2011 |publisher=International Humanist and Ethical Union |access-date=16 August 2013}}</ref>
* Humanist of the Year award (2009) [[American Humanist Association]]<ref name="AHA award"/>
* Top-ranked blog written by a scientist ([[Nature (journal)|''Nature'' science journal]], 2006)<ref name="topfiveblogs"/>
